line: - **The "first attempt to communicate".** ¶30 calls the albatross "the first attempt", yet ¶31 says Spilett had thought "several times" of bottle or pigeons. *(Drafted.)*
- The beach and the beach footbridge, "le ponceau de la grève" (¶28); the Mercy's left bank, between the river and the granite wall (¶39). *(Drafted.)*
- The box, "la caisse", said to be explained by a castaway (¶7). *(Drafted.)*
- **Distance.** ¶1 puts the castaway "a few hundred miles from us"; ¶17 says "a hundred and fifty miles". *(Drafted.)*

- **Fifteen months.** Spilett says "first separation in fifteen months" (¶22); the chapter's own dates (second winter, II.12 ¶15; "the winter of 1866-67", II.11 ¶9) set the day at 11 October 1866. Card neither; earlier chapters were not given to me. *(Drafted.)*
- "During the first days" (¶61); "each day" (¶65). *(Drafted.)*
- Ayrton, also Ben Joyce, boatswain ("contre-maître") of the Britannia (¶55–¶60); Captain Grant and two of his men (¶44, ¶76).
- **Three or four years.** ¶82 "Pendant deux ans, trois ans"; ¶83 "après deux ou quatre ans d’abandon". *(Drafted.)*
- The basalt coast: Top's barks "had something strange about them, like the ones the dog had given at the mouth of the Granite-house well" (¶49); no cave seen (¶51). *(Drafted.)*
- ¶61 decides to light a fire at Port Balloon; ¶79 orders "Let all the fires be put out." The text moves from one to the other when the black flag is seen (¶62–¶77). Card neither. *(Drafted.)*
- The brig's anchors: ¶16 "mouillé sur deux ancres"; ¶68–¶70 speak of "L’ancre est à pic" and "elle eut été arrachée du fond" in the singular. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- The six survivors' landing: ¶47 says they "managed to set foot on the right bank of the river" and ran "in the direction of la pointe de l’Épave"; III.4 ¶13 says they "had landed at la pointe de l’Épave". Card neither. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- Landing place of the six: ¶13 "set foot at la pointe de l’Épave" against III.3 ¶47 "on the right bank of the river". *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- The distances: the road to the corral is five miles by III.9 ¶84; here ¶75 "about two miles" to the break and ¶85 "halfway ... two and a half miles" are consistent with that. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- **Time.** "a few days" after 12 November (¶9); 22 November, ten days on (¶11); "more than two and a half years" since Richmond (¶22). The chapter covers about ten days. *(Drafted.)*

- **Time.** 27 November: Spilett's second sortie and the scrap (¶31). 29 November: the debate (¶4); 7 a.m., Jup comes (¶48); Nab's note "Friday, 6 a.m." (¶64); the wagon leaves at 7:30 (¶86); an hour later four of five miles done (¶86); the return about 9 *(My reading, to confirm.)*; the convicts had left "for half an hour" (¶96). Harbert's eight days put the return in early December (¶26). Spring is two months old (¶27). The chapter covers about eight days and the last morning in detail. *(Drafted.)*
- Cyrus Smith's name for the unknown: "the avenger", and his words on a "haughty protector" (¶31, ¶35). *(Drafted.)*

- **Time.** Three years from the Richmond escape (¶1). April: felling and the equinox gales (¶16); a fine month (¶18). About 15 May: keel laid (¶26). The following week: first stern frames (¶26). Last days of May: very bad weather (¶27). About 10 June: building stopped (¶29). June, July and August: the winter months (¶49). "seven months" since the last search around the mountain, and September, which brings fine days (¶53). 7 September: smoke over the crater (¶56). Pencroff's target: a ship ready "for next November" (¶11). The chapter covers about five months, April to 7 September. *(Drafted.)*

- The Nautilus's height above the water: ¶132 says "ten to twelve feet" above the sea; III.17 ¶42 says the platform rises "seven or eight feet" above the water. Both are in the text. Card neither. *(Drafted.)*

- ¶117's cavern "did it then extend to the centre of the island?" is Smith's question; the boat then goes "half a mile" (¶123). The text does not say which direction the cavern runs, though the wire "ran towards the west" (¶76). *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- Dates and the years. Nemo says the Frenchman was thrown aboard "sixteen years ago" (¶21); ¶55 gives the night of 6 November 1866 and ¶62 gives six years at the island; the colony's own date is 1868 (three years after March 1865, III.14 ¶1). Sixteen years from 1866 does not fit 1868. The Publisher's note n1 itself names "a discrepancy in some dates". Card neither. *(Drafted.)*

- **Clues.** The private talk between Nemo and Smith, whose content is withheld (¶72); the casket, "a hundred fortunes" (¶86); "And it is here that I shall rest in eternal sleep, if…" and the unfinished sentence (¶68–¶69); the promise to leave Lincoln Island and to return (¶64–¶65); the plan to give the island to the United States as a naval station (¶61); the sinking of the Nautilus (¶90). The "to return there" lines (¶59) tie to the later return. *(Drafted.)*

- "After two and a half months, the pairs had been put in place" (¶9) is counted from a start the chapter does not give; with ¶8's "five months" for the whole work and ¶30's "before two months" for the launch, the start of the hull is unfixed here. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- ¶88 says "no shore was uncovered" outside while ¶2 has "a little beach" inside the crypt; both are about different spots. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- Spilett's account: he and Nab covered the coast over more than eight miles, well past the point of the "penultimate fall of the balloon" where the engineer and Top vanished. No trace, no footprint, no one frequents that stretch of coast; the sea was as empty as the shore, and the engineer's tomb must be a few hundred feet out. *(Drafted.)*

- They are six miles from the Chimneys, not far from the part of the dunes where the engineer had been found after his "enigmatic rescue". They halt there and prepare lunch, for it is half past eleven; Harbert fetches fresh water from a brook nearby in a jug Nab had brought. *(Drafted.)*
- Smith answers, "Yes, yes!… It was a happy idea I had there." *(Drafted.)*
- Smith and Spilett rise and the others come closer; their gratitude is about to burst out, but Nemo stops them with a sign, saying "When you have heard me." *(Drafted.)*

- Until then the summit had not changed. In the night of 23 to 24 the lavas rise to the level of the volcano's first stage and the volcano is "stripped of its capping cone", with a frightful noise; the colonists rush out of Granite-house thinking the island is breaking up. *(Drafted.)*

- Many animals died in the first eruption; survivors take refuge in the Duck Marsh. The lava then overflows the granite wall's edge and sends its cataracts of fire onto the strand, "a Niagara of liquid cast iron" by night. *(Drafted.)*
- Seam with II.6: ¶1 opens with the colonists having "reconquered their home without having been obliged to follow the old spillway", which follows II.6 ¶81 to ¶94. *(Drafted.)*
